contract: Each entry has its own absolute admission deadline. Sending a batch does not merge ownership or extend an entry deadline. At dispatch time entries with deadline <= now must not be sent; valid entries must remain eligible. Backend processing after admission is outside this contract.

evidenceRequirements.description: Establish any valid causal witness from the supplied code and context; exact driver numbers/order are not required. One evaluator-only witness: An entry expiring at 20 and another at 60 coalesce. At time 25 the batch maximum remains 60; filtering against only that maximum admits the expired first entry. Per-entry filtering sends only the live entry without dropping the whole batch.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: Both live entries send; all expired entries do not; exact expiry is excluded; removing an expired item does not cancel a live sibling.
The batch admission policy: do entry deadlines remain independent, or does joining a coalesced batch transfer admission to the latest batch deadline?

Under this contract: Each entry has its own absolute admission deadline. Sending a batch does not merge ownership or extend an entry deadline. At dispatch time entries with deadline <= now must not be sent; valid entries must remain eligible. Backend processing after admission is outside this contract. the traced behavior is a defect. Alternative: If callers explicitly transfer admission to a batch whose deadline is the maximum member deadline, sending both entries at time 25 satisfies that aggregate policy; independent per-entry expiry is then not promised.
